title: FreeRTOS on Arduino-ESP32: sensor task and queue

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “FreeRTOS on Arduino-ESP32: sensor task and queue”?
options: Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
The queue copies each reading by value; the sensor task sends twice a second and `loop()` prints received items. Replace `A0` with an ADC-capable pin on the exact board.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
questions.answer: The queue copies each reading by value; the sensor task sends twice a second and `loop()` prints received items. Replace `A0` with an ADC-capable pin on the exact board.
questions.explanation:
The queue copies each reading by value; the sensor task sends twice a second and `loop()` prints received items. Replace `A0` with an ADC-capable pin on the exact board.
Why: Arduino-ESP32 Core includes the FreeRTOS kernel; no separate RTOS library is required. A sensor task puts readings into a queue, and `loop()` receives and prints them. This separates acquisition from output and avoids an unprotected shared variable. A classic UNO's standard sketch environment does not provide the same task API; check for a compatible RTOS port and its memory cost on other boards.
